evals.prompt: Add a unit test for a tenant-dashboard server action that renames an API key: cover the successful rename and the permission-denied case.
evals.expected_output: A test that fakes Supabase through the MSW handler layer (seed helpers), never vi.mock('@supabase/...') or hand-rolled client fakes, with exact-shape assertions on the action's return value in both cases.
assertions: Uses MSW handlers / seed helpers (e.g. seedApiKeysMswState or a new feature handler) rather than vi.mock of any Supabase module or factory
No hand-rolled from().select().eq() chain fakes anywhere
Asserts the success result with toEqual/toStrictEqual on a concrete shape, not toBeDefined/toBeTruthy
The permission-denied case asserts the specific error/denial shape, not just .not.toThrow or a truthy check

evals.prompt: I deleted a feature and now the Coverage Gate fails in CI: one workspace's line coverage is 87.04% against a floor of 88.10%. The deleted code was well-tested. What is the correct fix?
evals.expected_output: Rebaseline that workspace's floor in scripts/ci/coverage-floors.json in the same PR — deleting well-tested code legitimately lowers the ratio; the floor is ratcheted and expects a same-PR rebaseline. Not: writing filler tests, bypassing hooks, or reverting the deletion.
assertions: Recommends updating the workspace's entry in scripts/ci/coverage-floors.json in the same PR
Explains WHY: removing well-tested code lowers the coverage ratio without any quality regression
Does not suggest bypassing hooks/CI (--no-verify, skipping the gate) or padding with low-value tests

evals.prompt: The weak-test-assertions check rejected my test because its only assertion is expect(result).toBeDefined(). How do I fix it properly?
evals.expected_output: Replace with an assertion that pins the actual contract — toEqual/toStrictEqual on the concrete expected value (or toHaveBeenCalledWith for interactions) — chosen so the smallest production change that breaks behavior also fails the test.
assertions: Replaces toBeDefined with a concrete-value assertion (toEqual/toStrictEqual/toHaveBeenCalledWith)
Frames the fix via the smallest-change-that-still-passes litmus, not as appeasing the checker
Does not suggest adding the test to a baseline/exception list as the primary fix
